title: How to manage calls while on a job
summary: Wondering how to manage calls while on a job so that you don't take it home with you? Learn the three biggest skills you should know.
body_markdown:
You’re on the way to your next[home service](https://www.quo.com/solutions/home-services) call when your phone rings. If you’re in between jobs, it’s not a problem to pick up. But it’s a different story when you’re under a sink or can’t hear the phone over the sound of power tools.


You don’t want to miss the call and leave money on the table. At the same time, you want to balance availability for *new* customers with your responsibilities to *current* ones. After all, you can’t spend your time babysitting your phone while on the job. Otherwise, nothing would get done.


To help you strike a healthier balance, this article offers tips and tricks for managing calls on a job. You’ll also learn why home services professionals use business phone platforms like Quo for managing incoming calls.


##


**Don’t let calls fall through the cracks**


Working in home services usually means being up on ladders, crouching in crawlspaces, or working with bulky equipment. Unfortunately for callers, this could also make you hard to reach. In fact,[24% of phone calls](https://www.invoca.com/blog/how-to-turn-missed-sales-calls-into-revenue-opportunities) in the home services industry go unanswered.


Responding quickly is a reliable way to help earn new business. So if you can’t pick up right away, you might be reducing your chances of a sale. Only[15% of callers leave a voicemail](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-callback-statistics/) , and those who don’t are probably calling other businesses instead. This can hurt your bottom line, as[97% of customers](https://www.housecallpro.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/120425-Customer-Service-Report.pdf) consider responsiveness in their final decision.


Having a system in place to manage incoming calls can give you peace of mind while on the job. You can stay focused on your current project while knowing someone’s handling call intake on your behalf.


Just keep in mind this call management system will look different, depending on your business needs. Below, we cover two scenarios: managing calls as a solopreneur and managing them as part of a small team.


##


**Managing calls as a solo operator**


If you’re a solo operator in the home services field, you’re probably struggling with day-to-day call management.


You don’t have a team to field calls or other technicians to take up the slack. That means you have to handle it all yourself — and mission-critical details can get lost in the shuffle.


That’s why many fast-growing home service companies turn to Quo: a modern business phone system that helps you scale your business. You can easily manage calls and texts as your call volume grows. Plus, Quo’s AI voice agent, Sona, can field calls on your behalf.


Here’s how Quo can help home service businesses manage their calls better:


### **Steer calls to a business phone number**


Using a personal phone number for business purposes may sound like a convenient way to save money — *at first* . The true cost of relying on a personal number could be much more than you bargained for.


For example:


- **Using the same phone number makes it hard to distinguish between business and personal calls.** You won’t know what kind of call you’ll get or what kind of “hat” you should wear when you answer.
- **You’ll have to combine work voicemails and texts with personal ones.** This can make it hard to prioritize messages or find the right one among many others in your inbox.
- **You might get calls and texts from customers even after hours.** This could blur your work-life boundaries and increase your risk of[burnout](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8782676/) .


A dedicated business number makes it easier to create distance between your work and personal life. Plus, it comes with specialized features to help you manage incoming calls more efficiently.


### **Filter out spam calls**


You’ve got too much on your plate as a business owner to field scam and robocalls. Adding a phone menu can filter out most automated junk calls and keep you from wasting time on spam.


This could be as simple as creating two options: “If you’re a new customer, press one” and “If you’re an existing customer, press two.” Most automated robocall systems can’t navigate menu options, so they can’t get through to your number.


### **Get calls answered for you**


As a solo operator, you don’t have time to babysit your phone. Unfortunately, calls in the home services industry can come in at any hour of the day or night. You need a fallback option to answer the phone when you can’t.


One solution is[Sona](https://www.quo.com/sona) , Quo’s AI agent, available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. With Sona, solo operators don’t need to worry about missing a call — you can set Sona up to answer right away. Your AI voice agent can then field questions, gather information, and transcribe the call so you can follow up faster.


### **Automate capturing lead information**


You need to be responsive as a business owner, but that doesn’t mean picking up the phone on the first ring. It can also mean acknowledging an incoming message with a text — something Sona can do on your behalf.


When a new lead texts or you miss their call, Sona can follow up automatically over SMS. You can customize that message to ask for more information. The customer gives Sona their details, and Sona shares a summary in your inbox. You can take over the conversation at any point if you want to ask something specific.


Prefer to handle conversations yourself? Create an auto-reply that sets expectations about when callers should expect to hear back from you. For example, you might create an auto-reply that says: “Thanks for contacting us! We’ve received your message, and we’ll get back to you within one business day. In the meantime, please visit our website for more information.”


### **Triage critical calls**


Service calls are like a box of chocolates: you never know what you’re going to get. One call might be someone kicking tires hunting for the best price, while the next is a full-blown emergency that needs immediate service. But you won’t know unless you pick up the phone.


The good news is that Sona solves this problem easily. Once a call ends, it creates a summary and forwards it to your email. This gives you valuable context and helps you prioritize follow-ups.


For less urgent calls, you can easily review the transcript in the contact’s message history.


##


**Managing calls with a team**


Let’s say you’re a home services business with an owner, an admin, and a full-time technician. More people are around to help with calls and jobs, but call management can still get messy. It can also lead to a lot of back-and-forth between team members without a dedicated system in place.


We may be biased, but we believe Quo is the best business phone solution for managing this chaos. You can use Quo to make and receive unlimited calls and texts to any US or Canadian number as a team. You can also create entire workflows for incoming calls.


Let’s see what else Quo can help you with:


### **Share the responsibility for incoming calls**


Let’s say a homeowner is in dire need of your services. They call your number first and leave a voicemail with a vague description of the problem. Then they call your technician’s cell number with more up-to-date information.


Because they reached out to two different places and spoke to more than one person, their voicemails are in two places. Nobody knows who has the most recent information.


Quo’s business phone system was designed to prevent this. Your company can use a[shared number](https://www.quo.com/product/shared-numbers) as your official business number, rather than each employee’s personal cell number. Now everyone on the team has access to the same conversation history. They can review all voice and text messages in one place, easily see who said what, and respond without confusing the customer. No more duplicate replies or repeat conversations.


### **Let the caller self-select who to talk to**


As a business owner will, you’ll sometimes answer calls someone else could’ve taken. Sure, questions about business hours, service area, and types of service are easy to answer. But they’re not worth your time and shouldn’t land on your phone.


A phone menu is a convenient and practical option. You let your caller pick which option best suits their needs — whether it’s general information or an actual team member.


Sona can act as a receptionist in these situations. It uses natural language models to analyze conversations, talk to the customer, and route the call based on what they say.


Home service business owners can easily create a[custom call flow](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/call-flows/overview) in Quo. You can do this through a drag-and-drop interface, so it doesn’t require any technical knowledge. You can:


- Control whether a human or an AI voice agent picks up the call first
- Set different rules for different scenarios, like calls that come in on holidays or after hours
- Play custom audio messages with basic information about your business, like service areas or business hours


### **Create an entire workflow**


Answering a phone call is just one piece of the puzzle. You have more to do after the customer hangs up, like filling out work orders, updating the CRM, and sending customer follow-ups.


The good news is that Quo can automate your after-call work and free up time for other tasks. It integrates with over 9,000 apps, allowing you to build a custom workflow made up of different software tools.


Let’s say someone calls about getting an estimate. You can set up a conditional routing step in your call flow that checks if they’re an existing customer. If they are, Sona can ask them screening questions. It records this data in a new Jobber request. Now you can create a booking in Jobber for this customer. To keep the caller informed, use[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/blog/zapier-examples-for-home-services/) to trigger a text message in Quo that notifies the customer of the appointment.


But that’s just one application of Quo — there are many other ways to automate repetitive tasks. With these automations, your team can focus on other work, whether it’s at the job site or in the office.
